extraction.agency_name: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
extraction.parent_department: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

findings.title: PHPA Did Not Use Available Resources to Verify Applicant Income and to Identify Possible Third-Party Insurance for Certain Programs
findings.description: PHPA did not use available independent resources such as MABS or the National Directory of New Hires to verify applicant income or identify third-party insurance for BCCDTP, MADAP, and MADAP-Plus programs.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that PHPA implement procedures to use available resources, such as MABS and the aforementioned MCPA contract, to help verify applicant income and to identify any third-party insurance.

findings.title: PHPA Did Not Always Consider Critical Information When Redetermining Applicant Eligibility For One Program
findings.description: PHPA did not always consider critical information such as income and insurance data in BCCDTP renewal applications; testing of 13 applications disclosed issues with spouse income documentation, third-party insurance identification, and SSN recording for 5 applications with paid claims totaling approximately $1.1 million.

dollar_amounts.context: paid claims for related applicants during fiscal years 2011 through 2013

findings.recommendation: We recommend that PHPA record all critical information reported by applicants and use the information to evaluate continued applicant eligibility and the existence of third-party insurance; determine whether the aforementioned applicants were eligible and had third-party insurance, and take appropriate action.

findings.title: Access to Systems Used to Maintain Critical Information and Process Related Claims For Certain Programs Was Not Adequately Restricted
findings.description: PHPA did not adequately restrict user access to the MADAP system; employees had capabilities to record eligibility or process claims without independent approval, including some with incompatible duties.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that PHPA ensure a documented review of critical data recorded into the MADAP system is performed by independent supervisory personnel; separate incompatible duties that allowed employees to input individuals as eligible and to manually process related claims; eliminate capabilities to ensure employees can only perform duties required as part of their job responsibilities.

findings.title: PHPA Did Not Always Obtain Certain Necessary Documents to Establish Provider Eligibility and Did Not Conduct Periodic Eligibility Reassessments
findings.description: PHPA did not always obtain required documentation such as physician licenses or proof of liability insurance; testing disclosed 8 payments totaling $361,646 for services by unverified physicians, and periodic reassessments were not conducted resulting in expired or suspended licenses.

dollar_amounts.context: payments for services performed by physicians whose licenses were never verified

findings.recommendation: We recommend that PHPA at the time of application obtain documentation of licensure and insurance for all individual physicians and therapists as required by State regulations; periodically reassess provider eligibility; investigate the aforementioned instances of unverified, expired, or suspended licenses, and ensure that the required documentation is obtained and appropriate actions are taken.

findings.title: PHPA Lacked Adequate Procedures and Controls Over Certain Collections
findings.description: PHPA lacked adequate procedures over HIV Client Services and BCCDTP collections; segregation of duties was not maintained for collections and accounts receivable, verifications were not timely or complete, and large rebates were received by check instead of wire transfer.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that PHPA establish adequate controls over HIV Client Services and BCCDTP collections; ensure employees without access to collections maintain the related accounts receivable records; perform timely and complete deposit verifications that ensure all recorded collections were deposited; pursue the feasibility of receiving large collections via wire transfer.

extraction.agency_response_summary: PHPA generally concurred with the findings and recommendations. The agency noted that some controls were already in place or would be implemented via a new Medicaid Management Information System (MMIS), though implementation was delayed. PHPA indicated it would pursue feasibility of wire transfers for rebates and complete deposit verifications within 30 days.
extraction.extraction_notes: Report date derived from header 'March 2015'. Audit period covers PHPA/HSIA/OPR scope dates. Prior findings count based on combined preceding reports (IDEHA and Family Health). Dollar amounts converted to integers.
